description.narrative:
Since 2010, the Flexible Multi-Partner Mechanism (FMM) is FAO’s main pooled funding mechanism for resource partners willing to contribute flexible, voluntary and multi-year resources to the Organization for the achievement of results under FAO’s Strategic Framework and the realization of catalytic impacts.
The FMM has supports the development of innovative solutions for farmers and food producers and assists them in tackling emerging priorities.
. The FAO Multipartner Support Programme Mechanism (FMM) is a multisector project aimed at enhancing food security policy and administrative management. This program is a result of voluntary pluriannual contributions from multiple international partner organizations, as stated in the project profile. The rationale behind this project lies in the FAO's mandate to improve nutrition levels, agricultural productivity, and quality of life for populations whose livelihoods depend on renewable natural resources, and its vision of a world free from hunger and malnutrition. The FMM is also aligned with Belgium's commitment to allocate at least 50% of its Aid Public Development (APD) to Least Developed Countries (LDCs), as 12 out of the 14 partner countries of Belgium's Cooperation au Developpement are LDCs. The program also focuses on resilient and sustainable agriculture, a key aspect in achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and inclusive economic growth. The FMM aims to address challenges and crises while promoting good governance and common transversal themes such as the environment and gender equality. The partnership between Belgium and the FAO has a history of effective collaboration, particularly within development and humanitarian programs. This partnership is strengthened through regular dialogue and close cooperation between the two parties. The FMM seeks to operationalize this partnership for the full realization of the FAO's mandate and the objectives of Belgium's Cooperation au Developpement. The program aims to facilitate an operational partnership between the FAO and all Belgian actors involved, including public sector representatives, civil society, research centers, and universities. It also encourages complementarity between Belgium's bilateral and multilateral actions and those conducted with the FAO. The FMM intends to improve the exchange of political, strategic, and technical knowledge related to agriculture, food security, and other relevant areas.
